text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000214 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity group, but the few 99215 charts reviewed support the billed level, so the documentation is too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 excess is not explained by a sicker panel: the by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running roughly two to four times the all-provider share in every condition band, from 0 conditions to 5+. That is a pattern consistent with upcoding rather than case mix, and it sits alongside a heavy concentration of 99214 claims. Against that, all 6 documented 99215 claims were supported, including low-complexity claim C0108812 (hypertension only, documented as high MDM at 50 minutes), though 6 charts is far too few to clear the pattern. The 4 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence of possibly templated or inflated notes, not proof. A reviewer should first request more 99215 charts, prioritizing the sampled low-complexity claims (for example C0108863, C0109028 and C0109351, which have no chronic conditions). They should also check whether the MDM and time in supported notes like C0108812 reflect a genuinely complex visit or cloned text."}
